title: add adaptive spline baseline and hedged fallback sentinel
author: Marina Patel
description:
Summary: Introduces an adaptive spline-based baseline estimator for temporal nonstationarity and a lightweight hedged-fallback sentinel that automatically stages fallback traffic and graceful backpressure when small-but-persistent regressions are detected.
Motivation: existing canary detectors are brittle against slow drifts in traffic shape (diurnal load, request size shifts) which inflate false positives. The spline baseline models the smooth trend at multiple time-scales so the detector focuses on short-term deviations rather than long-running baselines. The hedged fallback sentinel provides a low-latency mitigation path: when the detector signals a soft regression, we simultaneously route a small hedged fraction of traffic to a fallback model/replica pool while continuing evaluation; if the hedge shows stable improvement we widen failover, otherwise we gracefully revert and record diagnostics.
Design highlights:
- Adaptive spline baseline: multiscale B-spline smoother with automatic knot density adaptation driven by traffic curvature; uses online incremental updates and O(1) amortized per-sample cost. Configurable windows: short (1m), mid (15m), long (3h).
- Residual whitening: residuals are normalized by a dynamic variance estimate to avoid spike sensitivity.
- Probabilistic drift detector: gaussian-mixture residual model with temporal decay; outputs a continuous anomaly score and calibrated p-value.
- Hedged fallback sentinel: traffic hedging controller that maintains a target hedge-rate (default 5%), runs A/B style evaluation on hedged traffic, collects latency/qps/quality metrics and computes an expected-value score for progressive failover.
- Graceful backpressure: when backend capacity is constrained, hedged controller enforces soft throttles and signals autoscaler hints.
- Observability: new dashboards and span tags: canary.spline_baseline.*, sentinel.hedge.*. Alerts for persistent hedges and high rollback churn.
Checklist:
- [x] Algorithm implementation
- [x] Unit tests for spline updater and detector
- [x] Integration test against synthetic diurnal traffic generator
- [x] Canary dashboard panels and alert rules
- [x] Docs: design doc and operator runbook
- [x] Performance microbench (latency overhead < 2%)
- [x] Safety: default-off hedging for mainline until opt-in
Deployment plan: landed feature behind feature flag perf.spline_baseline.enabled=false by default; canary rollout to perf-canary stage cluster for 48 hours using gradual ramp policy.
Related: builds on theory in ENG-9876; incident SUP-4321 motivated hedging fallback after 2026-01-28 degradation.

Notes on code: spline_estimator.py contains an incremental knot-adjustment routine, with a small bounded in-memory ring buffer per time-scale. Detector uses an exponential-decay window for moments and fits a two-component gaussian mixture online. Hedged controller exposes an HTTP control endpoint for dynamic hedge-rate tuning and emits prometheus metrics: perf_canary_hedge_rate, perf_canary_hedge_latency_ratio, perf_canary_hedge_quality_delta.

Expected outcomes: fewer false-positive rollbacks during diurnal drift; ability to mitigate small regressions without full failover.
Potential risks: hedging increases traffic to fallback replicas (cost); operator confusion if hedges are frequent — mitigated via runbook and alerting.
